title: Futures and margin
objectives: Follow daily settlement through a futures margin account.

screens.prose: A **futures contract** is a forward traded on an exchange. You go long one index future at 8,000 points. Each point is worth £10.00, so the smallest move, a tick of 0.5 points, is worth £5.00. At the close of day 1 the exchange settles the future at 7,960.
screens.question: What is your gain or loss for day 1?

hints.text: How many points did the future move, and which way?
It fell from 8,000 to 7,960: 40 points against you.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the change in points by £10.00 a point.

byKey.sign: You are long, so a fall is a loss. Use a negative number.
byKey.points: That is the move in points. Each point is worth £10.00.
byKey.tick: You valued each point at £5.00. That is one tick, half a point.

explain.text: The future fell 40 points, and you are long, so you lose $40 \times 10 = \text{£}400.00$. Unlike a forward, a future settles this loss tonight, in cash. Every evening the exchange moves the day's gain or loss between buyers and sellers.

screens.prose: To trade, you leave £6,000.00 with the exchange. Each evening it adds your gain or takes your loss. If the balance closes below £4,500.00, you must top it back up to £6,000.00 before the next day. Here is your balance over five days.
screens.question: Tap the day the exchange asks you for more cash.

hints.text: Find the dashed line at £4,500.00.
Only one evening closes under that line.
Day 3 closes at £4,300.00, below £4,500.00.

feedback.correct: Day 3: the balance closes at £4,300.00, below £4,500.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Look for the evening the balance closes below £4,500.00, not below £6,000.00.

byKey.d1: Day 1 closes at £5,600.00. That is below the £6,000.00 you started with, but above £4,500.00.
byKey.d4: Day 4 is back at £6,000.00: that jump is your top-up after day 3.
byKey.d5: Day 5 closes at £6,500.00, above both lines.

explain.text: Days 1 and 2 dip below £6,000.00, but the rule is the £4,500.00 line. Day 3 closes at £4,300.00, so you pay in enough to restore £6,000.00. The jump on day 4 is that payment.

screens.prose: The £6,000.00 is the **initial margin**; £4,500.00 is the **maintenance margin**. Settling gains and losses each evening is **marking to market**. The demand to top up is a **margin call**. On day 3 your balance closed at £4,300.00.
screens.question: How much must you pay in after day 3?

hints.text: A margin call restores the balance to one of the two lines. Which one?
The call tops the account up to the initial margin, £6,000.00.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Top the balance up to the initial margin.

byKey.maint: You topped up to the maintenance level. A call restores the initial margin, £6,000.00.
byKey.whole: You paid the whole initial margin again. The £4,300.00 is still yours; you only fill the gap.
byKey.loss: That is day 3's loss. The call fills the gap from £4,300.00 up to £6,000.00.

explain.text: The call is $6{,}000 - 4{,}300 = \text{£}1{,}700.00$, back up to the initial margin. The trigger is the maintenance line; the target is the initial line. The gap between them saves you a call on every small loss.

screens.prose: Now build the account yourself, one contract at £10.00 a point. Balance means after the evening's settlement, before any top-up. A top-up lands before the next day starts. Day 1 is done.
screens.question: Fill in days 2 to 5. Losses are negative; write 0 where there is no call.

hints.text: Each day: points moved times £10.00, added to the last balance plus any top-up.
Day 3 is the first balance below £4,500.00.

feedback.correct: One call, £1,700.00 after day 3; the week ends at £6,500.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work one row at a time, and check each balance against £4,500.00.

byKey.r1c2: Day 2 moves from 7,960 to 7,900: 60 points down, at £10.00 a point.
byKey.r1c3: Start from day 1's £5,600.00 and take off day 2's loss.
byKey.r2c4: Day 3 closes at £4,300.00, below £4,500.00. Top it up to £6,000.00.
byKey.r3c2: The price did not move on day 4, so nothing is settled.
byKey.r3c3: Day 4 starts at £6,000.00 after your £1,700.00 top-up. With no price change, it stays there.
byKey.r4c3: Day 5 starts from £6,000.00, not from £4,300.00: the top-up is in the account.

explain.text: The losses of days 2 and 3 take the balance to £4,300.00, and the call restores £6,000.00. Day 4 has no price change, so nothing moves at all. Day 5's gain lifts you to £6,500.00, and you may withdraw the £500.00 above the initial margin.

screens.prose: Someone is short the contract you bought. Their account also starts at £6,000.00, with the same margin rules. The exchange passes your losses to them each evening.
screens.question: What is the short's balance at the close of day 3?

hints.text: Your loss is the short's gain.
Over three days you lost $400 + 600 + 700$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add your three losses to the short's £6,000.00.

byKey.copied: You gave the short your balance. A fall that hurts the long helps the short.
byKey.start: The short's account is marked to market too. Each evening it receives your loss.
byKey.day: That counts only day 3's gain. Add all three days.

explain.text: The short gains what you lose: £1,700.00 over three days, so £7,700.00. Your call money went, through the exchange, to cover their side. Futures, like forwards, create no money; they move it daily.

screens.prose: A new week, the same rules: initial £6,000.00, maintenance £4,500.00. The future settles at 7,930, 7,840, 7,900 and 7,880. A colleague adds the week's moves: −120 points, or −£1,200.00. That leaves £4,800.00, above £4,500.00, so no call, he says.
screens.question: How much margin did the long actually pay in during the week?

widget.label: Margin paid in during the week

hints.text: Settle the account evening by evening, not once at the end.
After day 2 the balance is $6{,}000 - 700 - 900$.
Day 2 closes at £4,400.00, below £4,500.00: a call of £1,600.00. Days 3 and 4 never drop below again.

feedback.correct: Day 2 closes at £4,400.00, so the long pays £1,600.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the balance each evening and check it against £4,500.00.

byKey.end: You settled the week in one go, as the colleague did. Futures settle every evening, and day 2 closed at £4,400.00.
byKey.maint: You topped up only to the maintenance level. A call restores the initial margin, £6,000.00.
byKey.loss: That is the week's net loss. The call depends on the balance on the worst evening.
byKey.two: Day 1 loses 70 points, £700.00, and day 2 loses 90, £900.00. Check day 2's balance again.

explain.text: Day 1 takes £700.00, leaving £5,300.00. Day 2 takes £900.00, leaving £4,400.00, below £4,500.00: a call for £1,600.00. Later gains cannot undo a call that fell due on day 2.

screens.prose: You settled each evening. For $n$ contracts at $m$ pounds a point, with settlement prices $F_t$: $$G_t = n\,m\,(F_t - F_{t-1}), \qquad B_t = B_{t-1} + G_t.$$ If $B_t$ falls below the maintenance margin, you pay in enough to restore the initial margin.
screens.question: Why does the exchange settle every day, rather than once at delivery?

options.text: So no one can owe more than about one day's move, and a default costs little
To pay winners their profits sooner
options.why: Profits arriving sooner is a side effect. The point is that losses cannot pile up unpaid.

options.text: To keep the futures price equal to the spot price
options.why: Settlement moves cash; it does not set the price. The future meets spot only at expiry.

options.text: To charge a fee every day
options.why: Settlement is not a fee. The cash goes from one side's account to the other's.

feedback.correct: Daily settlement caps what any side can owe at about one day's loss.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about a forward whose loser owes a year of losses on one day.

explain.text: A forward's loser may owe a year of losses on the delivery date, and might not pay. Daily settlement collects each loss within a day, with the margin as a cushion. The exchange's clearing house stands between buyer and seller, so neither faces the other's credit risk.

screens.prose: The **basis** is the spot price minus the futures price. Four weeks before expiry the index is at 7,990 and the future at 8,010. On the expiry day the future settles at the index's own level.
screens.question: What is the basis on the expiry day?

hints.text: What price does the future settle at on its last day?
At expiry the future is set from the index itself.
Spot minus a future equal to spot is 0.

feedback.correct: The two meet at expiry: a basis of 0.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. On the last day the future settles at the index level.

byKey.stuck: That is today's basis, $7{,}990 - 8{,}010$. It shrinks as expiry nears.
byKey.sign: The basis is spot minus future, and at expiry the two are equal.

explain.text: Before expiry the gap is the cost of carry, and it shrinks as the time left shrinks. At expiry the future settles at the index, so the basis is 0: **convergence**.

screens.prose: A pension fund holds £800,000.00 of shares that track the index. It hedges with a short position in 10 futures, at £10.00 a point. Its margin account holds £60,000.00, with maintenance at £45,000.00. One day the index rallies 250 points.
screens.question: How much cash must the fund pay in the next morning?

hints.text: The fund is short, so a rally is a loss on the futures.
The loss is $10 \times 250 \times \text{£}10.00$, taken from £60,000.00.
The balance falls to £35,000.00, below £45,000.00: top up to £60,000.00.

feedback.correct: A £25,000.00 loss leaves £35,000.00, so the call is £25,000.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the futures loss, the new balance, and the gap to £60,000.00.

byKey.offset: The shares did gain about as much, but that gain is not cash. The margin call must be paid in cash, tomorrow.
byKey.maint: You topped up to the maintenance level. A call restores the initial margin, £60,000.00.
byKey.one: That is one contract's loss. The fund is short 10.

explain.text: The futures lose $10 \times 250 \times 10 = \text{£}25{,}000.00$, leaving £35,000.00, so the fund pays £25,000.00. The shares gained about as much, but only on paper, so a hedger needs cash ready. In 1993 Metallgesellschaft's US arm met such calls on an oil hedge, then closed out about 1.3 billion dollars down.

ideas: A future is a forward traded on an exchange and settled every evening: each day's gain or loss moves in cash.
A margin call comes when the balance closes below the maintenance margin, and it restores the initial margin.
Daily settlement limits what anyone can owe to about a day's move. The future converges to spot at expiry.

formula.name: Marking to market
formula.note: Below maintenance, pay in up to the initial margin.

summary.trap: Settle every evening, not once at the end. A call due on a bad day is not cancelled by later gains.

quiz.prose: You are long 2 futures at £10.00 a point. Today's settlement price falls from 7,500 to 7,470.
quiz.question: What is today's gain or loss on your account?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply contracts, pounds a point and the change in points.

byKey.one: That is one contract. You hold 2.
byKey.sign: You are long and the price fell, so it is a loss.
byKey.points: That is the move in points. Multiply by £10.00 and by 2 contracts.

explain.text: Each contract loses 30 points at £10.00, which is £300.00, and you hold 2. The account is debited £600.00 tonight.

quiz.prose: Your initial margin is £6,000.00 and the maintenance margin £4,500.00. Your balance is £5,000.00. Tonight you lose £300.00.
quiz.question: How large is the margin call?

feedback.correct: £4,700.00 is above the maintenance line: no call.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the new balance with the maintenance margin.

byKey.initial: You compared the balance with the initial margin. The call comes only below £4,500.00.
byKey.loss: The loss is settled from your balance. A call comes only when the balance closes below maintenance.

explain.text: The balance falls to £4,700.00, still above £4,500.00. No call is made; the margin between the two lines absorbs the loss.

quiz.prose: Same rules: initial £6,000.00, maintenance £4,500.00. Your balance is £4,600.00, and tonight you lose £400.00.
quiz.question: How large is the margin call?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the new balance, then the gap up to the initial margin.

byKey.maint: You topped up to the maintenance line. A call restores the initial margin.
byKey.loss: That replaces tonight's loss only. The call fills the whole gap to £6,000.00.
byKey.none: £4,200.00 is below £4,500.00, so a call is due.

explain.text: The balance closes at £4,200.00, below £4,500.00. You pay $6{,}000 - 4{,}200 = \text{£}1{,}800.00$ to restore the initial margin.

quiz.prose: A month before expiry an index future trades 25 points above the index.
quiz.question: What happens to that gap by the expiry day?

options.text: It shrinks to zero: the future settles at the index

options.why: You kept today's gap. It is the cost of carry for a month, and that cost shrinks with the time left.

options.text: It grows as traders bet on the index
options.why: Bets move both prices. At expiry the future is defined by the index itself.
At expiry the future and the index are the same thing, so arbitrage closes any gap.

feedback.correct: Convergence: the basis is 0 at expiry.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask how the future's final settlement price is set.

explain.text: The gap reflects the carry over the time left, which falls to nothing at expiry. The future's last settlement price is the index, so the two meet.
